newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Bulog says to buy 30,000 tonnes of CPO.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Bulog says to buy 30,000 tonnes of CPO.

text.p: Indonesian commodities regulator Bulog said on Wednesday it planned to buy an additional 30,000 tonnes of crude palm oil from state-owned plantations in an effort to stabilise olein prices in the domestic market.

"In the effort to stabilise prices in the domestic market in the coming months, several steps are required such as ... strengthening the reserves by buying an additional 30,000 tonnes of CPO," Bulog chairman Beddu Amang told members of parliament.
Crude palm oil (CPO) is the raw material for making palm olein.
Amang said olein prices had increased sharply by 185 rupiah/kg to 1,500 rupiah/kg in the third week of August against 1,315 rupiah in late July.
Olein was quoted at 1,440 rupiah/kg in Medan, 1,470 rupiah in Jakarta and 1,460 rupiah in Surabaya on Wednesday. CPO was last traded at 1,240 rupiah/kg.
Amang said Bulog planned to buy the additional CPO from state-owned plantations and not from private firms as these firms prefered to export their products.
The state regulator will also issue new regulations on the effective date of monthly CPO export taxes to reduce exports and increase supply in the domestic market in the coming months, Amang said.

"The export tax for September 1996 will be based on the bill of loading date and not on the announcement date of the export so that the "zero" export tax should only be effective until late August 1996," he said.
Bulog had a zero tax on CPO exports in August and a tax of $34.16/tonne in September. Amang did not say if the new regulation would also apply to export taxes on olein.

The taxes, which were introduced in September 1994 in an attempt to reduce exports and maintain supplies to the domestic market, are based on an composite average of international prices in the last two weeks of the previous month.

Recent comments from economists and politicians urging the government to reduce or abolish the CPO export tax were not relevant as it was not in line with moves to stabilise olein prices in the domestic market, Amang said.
Bulog had imported 20,000 tonnes of olein to help ease prices in the domestic market, with the first shipment having arrived on September 8, and planned to import more if necessary, he said.
The commodity regulator will continue its market operations to gradually reduce olein prices in the domestic market to 1,400 rupiah/kg or even lower, he said.
